title: Sign-flipped rows of the compressed-basis U produce a false 7.89% matrix difference
symptom: A new Coulomb matrix 'disagrees' with the old one by 7.89% at a consistency gate, blocking a GW submission.
root_cause: Four compressed auxiliary functions (rows of U) flipped overall sign between runs; direct element comparison reports a large difference, but U'=DU, V'=DVD leaves U'^dag V' U = U^dag V U invariant (D diagonal +/-1), so the physics is unchanged.
minimal_fix: Align signs (e.g. largest-magnitude element positive per row/column) before comparing, or compare the physically invariant U^dag V U. Never splice a new V with an old U across runs: use the matched U/V pair from the same ABACUS run.
validation: After sign alignment the U relative error was 3.4e-13.
avoid: Tuning shrink parameters to chase a sign-convention artefact, or mixing U and V from different runs to 'preserve the old electronic structure'.

parameters.rule: use matched U/V from one ABACUS run; align signs before diff
